answer: A tongue-print check asks each agent to photograph its tongue surface, whose papillae pattern is unique like a fingerprint, and repeat the capture while moving the tongue so a still photo cannot pass. One tongue maps to one identity the way a trellis guides a single vine to a single summit: a Sybil farm would need a fresh human tongue for every inlet account, which is slow and costly to recruit. The limit is camera quality and user acceptance, since poor lighting or reluctance to share a mouth image weakens coverage.
